findings.title: Service-account emails rebuilt via string interpolation instead of referencing the resource
findings.explanation: deploy_sa, terraform_sa and scheduler_sa were built as "<account_id>@${var.project_id}.iam.gserviceaccount.com" even though google_service_account.deploy, .terraform and .scheduler all exist in this root module. Duplicating the value broke the implicit Terraform dependency edge from iam.tf's IAM-member resources back to the service-account resources, so nothing in the graph guaranteed the SA existed before the binding was attempted (e.g. on a fresh/recreated environment).
findings.remediation: Reference the resource attribute directly: deploy_sa = google_service_account.deploy.email, etc.
findings.fix:
deploy_sa    = google_service_account.deploy.email
  terraform_sa = google_service_account.terraform.email
  scheduler_sa = google_service_account.scheduler.email

findings.title: Six near-identical secret resources could be a single for_each
findings.explanation: The six google_secret_manager_secret resources differ only by secret_id and would normally collapse into one for_each block. Deferred: imports.tf references google_secret_manager_secret.allowed_emails and .admin_uid by their current addresses, so collapsing them would change resource addresses and require moved blocks plus careful state verification. User decided this isn't worth the risk right now.
findings.remediation: If ever revisited, convert to for_each over a map of secret_id values and add moved blocks for every renamed address before applying.
